items.title: A criterion reducing a property of coherent sheaves on a Noetherian algebraic space to its behaviour on irreducible supports
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is a criterion reducing a property of coherent sheaves on a Noetherian algebraic space to its behaviour on supports: two out-of-three for short exact sequences, descent from finite direct sums, and a supply of sheaves on every reduced irreducible closed subspace, together force the property for all coherent sheaves (statement lines 2651-2677). The proof picks a minimal counterexample support, rules out reducible supports by an extension argument, filters away the powers of the ideal of the support, and in the irreducible case compares the given sheaf with the sheaf supplied by condition (3) over a nonempty open, extending the comparison by Artin-Rees and finishing with conditions (1) and (2). The minimal-counterexample reduction and the comparison over an open are the substance, so the claim is H2.
